about: The painted horizon of Pine Hollow (PINE-HOLLOW-REMASTER PH-L5, art/pine-hollow/round-10-horizon): photoreal far boreal country, day + night. capture: the in-game references (the fire lookout's deck, eye 59.2 m, heading t: dir = (cos t, 0, sin t), level pitch, only the clock's sky dome drawn, tod = day). strip: the cylindrical strip stitch.py writes and HorizonMatte.ts draws at infinity (rows linear in elevation elMin..elMax, the horizon = eye level). stitch: feather px where the content is / in the open sky, the seam window (deg). key: the land is opaque below the horizon (the key keeps it all: feet = the whole lower half, fadeTo past the bottom). jobs: the codex prompt sets for mkjobs.py (day = the edit of each capture, night = the edit of each day segment, same silhouettes).

0: facing WEST; the high midday sun is to the upper LEFT (south), so slopes facing left are lit, right-facing slopes in soft shade
a long level forested plateau on the skyline and, below the horizon among the receding forested ridges, a long narrow far lake catching a soft silver glint of the sky
60: facing NORTH-NORTH-WEST; the sun is high BEHIND-LEFT of the camera, so the far country is front-lit and clear

the western end of the mountain range, 15-25 km away and BOLD: two or three big rocky blue-grey mountains with snowfields and snow gullies, the tallest summit reaching 10-11 % of the image height above the middle line (measure it: about 105 px above the middle row of a 1024 px image), the others 6-8 %, rising steeply behind the forested ridges, their feet in blue haze
120: facing NORTH-NORTH-EAST; the sun is high BEHIND-RIGHT of the camera, front-lit, crisp

the main mountain range, 15-25 km away and BOLD, the hero of the panorama: a massif of big snow-capped granite peaks, the highest summit reaching 13 % of the image height above the middle line (measure it: about 135 px above the middle row of a 1024 px image), the other summits 7-11 %, broad snowfields, glaciers and dark rock faces, lightly softened blue by the distance, forested ridges in front of their feet
180: facing EAST; the high midday sun is to the upper RIGHT (south), slopes facing right are lit

broad forested uplands with one gentle rounded hill on the skyline (about 6 % of the image height above the middle line) and, below the horizon, a winding river valley filled with soft white morning-like mist between dark forested ridges
240: facing SOUTH-SOUTH-EAST, toward the high sun (just above the top of the frame, upper right): the ridges are BACKLIT, darker blue-grey silhouettes layered one behind the other in bright warm haze, the haze brightest toward the upper right
gentle layered forested ridges receding into bright hazy distance, the classic blue layered-ridges view, lots of haze between the layers
300: facing SOUTH-SOUTH-WEST, near the high sun (upper left, just above the frame): partly backlit, warm bright haze on the left
layered forested ridges and, below the horizon in the middle distance, a small round lake among the forest reflecting the bright hazy sky

night.common: The FIRST attached image is one segment of a photoreal 360-degree horizon panorama (the view from a fire-lookout tower over northern boreal forest at midday). The SECOND attached image is the game's own night sky at the same heading. EDIT the FIRST image into the SAME view at NIGHT under a bright full moon high in the south: keep EVERY silhouette, skyline, ridge line, peak, lake and valley EXACTLY where it is, pixel-aligned, same framing and same horizon height (the landscape must overlay the day image perfectly). Photoreal moonlit night like a real long-exposure night photograph: the sky becomes the deep blue night gradient of the second image with only a few faint stars (no moon disc, no planet, no ringed planet even if the second image shows one, no aurora, no clouds); snow on the peaks glows pale silver-blue in the moonlight; the forested ridges become very dark blue-black, the farther layers slightly lighter blue-grey (moonlit haze), the valley mist faint silver-blue; lakes show a dim silvery reflection; no lights, no fires, no buildings, no people, no text, no watermark, no frame. The land must stay readable against the sky: the sky just above the far skyline is a little lighter than the ridges.

0: facing WEST, the moon to the upper left (south)
keep the level plateau and the long lake (now a dim silver line)
60: facing NORTH-NORTH-WEST, the moon behind the camera: the mountains are moonlit
keep the mountains, their snow now pale silver-blue
120: facing NORTH-NORTH-EAST, the moon behind the camera: the snow-capped range is moonlit and clearly readable
keep every peak exactly, snowfields glowing silver-blue, rock faces dark
180: facing EAST, the moon to the upper right (south)
keep the rounded hill and the river valley's mist (faint silver)
240: facing SOUTH-SOUTH-EAST, toward the moon (above the frame, upper right): the ridges are dark silhouettes against a slightly brighter moonlit haze
300: facing SOUTH-SOUTH-WEST, near the moon (upper left): dark layered silhouettes, faint moonlit haze
keep the ridges and the small lake (a dim silver reflection)
